method: scripts/dev/roll_check.py sweep. The world is never modified: a throwaway sibling .omnisim_roll_<stem>.wbt is written next to it with every controller swapped to the uniform `roll_drive` and a `roll_probe` supervisor appended, then deleted. Wheel spin is read as (omega_wheel - omega_chassis) . axis_world through the supervisor API; body speed is projected on axis_world x up. Medians over a 500-step window after an 80-step settle, restricted to the samples where the robot was actually moving. Verdicts branch on the SIGN of the residual: ROLLING / SLIDING (body outruns the wheels -- the defect) / WHEELSPIN (wheels outrun the body) / REVERSED / IDLE / NO_DATA. Full write-up: docs/developer/roll-check.md.

projects/languages/cpp/worlds/example.wb.note: FIXED 2026-08-10 (basicTimeStep <= 8 + newtonSubsteps 4) but not yet clean. The fix removed the launch: peak body speed 12.623 -> 0.138 m/s, and the wheels now turn at the commanded rate instead of a garbage one. The residual is the robot creeping against the wall of a very small arena while its wheels keep turning -- WHEELSPIN, not the sliding defect. Re-grading the same samples over the first 1.2 s (before the wall) moves several of these to ROLLING, which is evidence the wheels are fine and the arena is short.

projects/robot_combat/battlebots/worlds/.note: MULTI-ROBOT ARENA -- inconclusive by construction, NOT a world defect. The sweep drives every robot forward at once, so they reach each other and the arena walls inside the window; the body-speed side of the ratio then measures the collision, not the wheels. Every robot's wheels track the commanded rate. The isolated equivalent of this chassis, projects/robot_combat/worlds/tests/drive_test.wbt, measures ROLLING at 0.001 slip. Grading these properly needs a one-robot-at-a-time protocol that does not exist yet.
